ratings_why.fun: Borrowed shape on off-tribe engines, the Hare in the Moon, Waxwell and The Three Hares give real placement and timing puzzles every turn; the low tiers are plainer.
ratings_why.distinct: A public moon cycle you bend, plus Hares that copy other tribes' text at Full, plays unlike today's tribes, though the Waxing and Charmer buffs are familiar.

verdict_why: Whether a Hare can copy text another Hare borrowed is unsettled, and the coven build depends on the answer.

points.text: Under Mother Meikle Care, build A says a row of Hares all copy one Hedgerow passer, but it also says two Changelings side by side get nothing from each other. Say whether a Hare copies the text its left neighbour borrowed (a chain) or only printed text.
Dame Waxwell turning twice with Mother Meikle Care out: say whether Meikle's turn to Full happens between Waxwell's two turns, so New lands on Full then Waning, or on Full.
Changeling Sister copying Mad March Hare or Suitor Jack on the turn to Full is a lovely hidden combo; a build line naming the Moonturn-on-Full copy would show players it exists.
Spring Jill does nothing three fights in four. A small New or Waning line, such as boxing when alone in its row, would tie it into Hare in Her Form's row play.

Leveret in the Form wants no Hare beside it while Suitor Jack wants to sit beside his target; letting Jack's left be a Leveret's space across rows would make that clash a choice instead of a dead slot.

standouts.why: Copying an Ooze's Eat or Old Wat's death trigger at Full is the tribe's best Johnny moment.
The Three Hares turns any neighbour's growth, Hare or not, into three-way growth, and combos with Suitor Jack and Eat.
Sister Silverpenny borrowing the enemy's text, doubled by the Moon-Scour at Full, is a wild read-the-opponent card.

weakest.why: Spring Jill is a vanilla body outside Full.
Dew-Pond Scryer only turns the Moon once; it has no other hook.
Hare's-Foot Charmer is a generic adjacency buffer with a phase number bolted on.

flags.note: Golden Waxwell, golden Hare in the Moon and golden Mad March Hare multiply to about 270 stats a turn, as the risks say.
Jill Longshanks chains Boxes off each win and grows every winning Hare; against a weak board she can clear it at Start of Combat.
Whether Borrowed shape granted by Meikle Care chains through a row of Hares is not stated.
